name: Small Bets
tagline: Community and live classes for people building a portfolio of small online bets

revenue.label: $824K community revenue over its first 24 months (Nov 2021-Oct 2023)

team: Solo until July 2023, then run as a partnership with Louie Bacaj
summary: Daniel Vassallo left a ~$500K/yr Amazon Web Services job and ran several small products instead of one startup: an AWS book, a $25 Twitter audience course, a $375 cohort course, and the Small Bets community with a one-time lifetime fee. Small Bets made $824,409 revenue in its first two years, and he sold it to Gumroad for $3.6M in April 2025.
origin: After leaving AWS, Vassallo co-wrote 'The Good Parts of AWS' (launched on Gumroad on Dec 25, 2019 at $65) and in April 2020 released a $25 video course, 'Everyone Can Build a Twitter Audience', that took about 16 hours to make. He then ran a $375 two-week Small Bets cohort course over Zoom, and gave students lifetime access to a Discord. That Discord became the Small Bets community in November 2021.
howItMakesMoney: Mainly one-time payments for lifetime membership to Small Bets (live events from members and guest speakers, community chat on Discord, recordings, course deals). The lifetime price has moved between about $185 and $245 with Black Friday promotions, and a one-year $99 option was added in November 2023. Earlier income came from the $25 Twitter course and the AWS book.
growth: Leaving a ~$500K/yr job to work independently gave him a story that drew early attention
Shared exact revenue and hours per product publicly on X, which became marketing
The $25 Twitter course (13,000+ sales, ~$310K) proved his audience would buy
The $375 cohort course sold out week after week ($150K from 400 customers in 5 months) and seeded the community
Paid members and guest experts (typically $1,000 a session) to teach live events, adding content without him producing it all
Ran pricing experiments on the lifetime fee, especially on Black Friday; November 2023 was the first $100K revenue month
Word of mouth and a small affiliate program (20% referral fee)
moat: Community network effects (thousands of lifetime members and member-run events) plus Vassallo's personal following and public track record.
risks: Lifetime pricing means little recurring revenue; income depends on continuous new members. Much of the value was tied to the founder, which is why the Gumroad deal requires him to keep running it for five years.

timeline.event: Launches 'The Good Parts of AWS' on Gumroad; $45K in 14 days
Launches $25 'Everyone Can Build a Twitter Audience' course on Gumroad
Reports Small Bets: 500 hours for $545,072 profit; Twitter course: 16 hours for $270,971 profit
First $100K revenue month, driven by a Black Friday offer
Sells Small Bets to Gumroad for $3.6M (50% cash, 50% stock options), 6,692 members; about 8x 2024 profit

lessons: Measure each product by profit per hour invested, not MRR
A cheap, fast product (a 16-hour video course) can validate an audience before a larger bet
Communities scale when members teach each other, not just the founder
Transparency about numbers can be the marketing for a business-advice product
A lifetime-fee community can still be sold if membership and content are documented

rebuild.idea: A lifetime-fee community and class series for early-career public servants or NGO staff building side incomes within their employer's ethics rules
rebuild.why: Most indie-business communities assume tech workers; government and nonprofit staff face specific conflict-of-interest rules and have no dedicated space.
mvp: Write one public post about your own side income under those constraints
Run a free live session on what is and isn't allowed, collect emails
Offer a $99 lifetime founding membership with 4 scheduled live classes
Invite 2 members to teach classes on their own side projects
rebuild.fit: Someone who has worked in that sector and already runs a small permitted side project
rebuild.pricing: One-time lifetime membership at $99 for founding members, raised in steps toward $199-$249 as the recorded class library grows, with an optional $49/year tier.
rebuild.market: Buyers are early-career public servants and NGO staff who want permitted side income, reached through LinkedIn, sector newsletters and alumni networks of public-policy schools. Competitors are general indie-business communities such as Small Bets and Indie Hackers, plus free Reddit and Facebook groups.
